St. Constantine the Great

Saints

Saint Constantine the Great

St. Constantine the Great · St. Constantine I · St. Constantine Equal to the Apostles · St. Emperor Constantine

Period
Third century–337; reign 306–337
Region
Roman Empire; Constantinople
Titles / vocation
Equal to the Apostles · Ruler
Commemoration
May 21

Introduction

Saint Constantine was the Roman emperor associated with Christianity’s legal freedom, the founding of Constantinople, and the First Ecumenical Council. His feast is shared with Saint Helena.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death in 337 after Baptism; not a martyr

Read circumstances and sources

Background

He was the son of Constantius Chlorus and Saint Helena. After his father’s death in 306, the army acclaimed him emperor at York. The OCA life situates his rise within the divided Roman imperial government.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Opening paragraphs on parents, imperial divisions and accession

Life and notable events

The life recounts a vision of the Cross before military victory. The settlement at Milan in 313 protected Christian religious practice. In 325 he convened the Council of Nicaea, where bishops condemned Arianism and confessed the Son’s full divinity.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on the sign of the Cross, Milan and the First Council

Death and martyrdom

He received Baptism near the end of his life and died in 337. His burial was in Constantinople’s church of the Holy Apostles. The ecclesiastical account describes death after Baptism, not a martyr’s execution.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Closing paragraphs on Baptism, repose and burial

Writings and legacy

The title Equal to the Apostles identifies the Church’s commemoration of his role in supporting Christianity. His mother has a separate Saint profile; their shared feast recalls their related but distinct service to the Church.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Title and paragraphs on imperial patronage and the Council
